purpose: Quantify whether qmirror QRNG sub-sampling reduces eval-score variance vs classical PRNG, on Llama-3.2-3B base @ HellaSwag.

design_pivot.actual_design: ONE full HellaSwag eval (10042 docs, ~2-3h) + 1000 offline index sub-samples (free); identical statistical power, 10× cheaper
design_pivot.key_lm_eval_finding: lm-eval-harness limit=N takes the FIRST N docs in fixed order regardless of random_seed (verified by reading lm_eval/api/task.py::doc_iterator). To get true seed-driven sub-sampling, we must pass an explicit `samples=[idx_list]` OR pre-sample indices and aggregate from full per-example correctness. We chose the latter (single GPU run).

honest_caveats_pre_results: Live qmirror entropy = HMAC-DRBG seeded by IonQ Forte 1 quantum measurement (4096 bits, 2026-05-02). This is the canonical production stream per nexus_qmirror_nist verdict, but it is a DETERMINISTIC EXPANSION of a single quantum sample — it shares the entropy bottleneck. A live ANU vacuum-fluctuation tap would give true per-bit quantum entropy; that hardware was unavailable. So this test compares 'quantum-seeded HMAC-DRBG' vs 'CPU PRNG', not 'live QRNG' vs 'CPU PRNG'.

Theoretical baseline expectation: when both sources draw uniform-without-replacement sub-samples of the same size from the same population, the variance of the sample mean is identical (≈p(1-p)/n × finite-population-correction). Any difference < 5% would fall within Monte-Carlo noise of N=500 sub-samples. F-QBENCH-1 is therefore a NULL hypothesis test where PASS is the surprising outcome — we expect FAIL even on a perfect QRNG, and FAIL is consistent with both 'qmirror works correctly' and 'qmirror is broken'.

Single benchmark (HellaSwag), single model (Llama-3.2-3B base 4-bit), single sub-sample size (500). MMLU was in the brief but skipped this cycle: MMLU is a 57-subtask group with N=12173 — variance on a sub-sample mean of 500 is dominated by subject-imbalance noise, not seed source, which would mask any QRNG signal. A separate cycle should run MMLU stratified-per-subject if needed.
